sections.content: The imperfecto is useful for describing food traditions in the past: what people usually ate, how meals were prepared and what the setting was like. It gives background rather than presenting each event as a separate completed action. Combine it with time expressions and a specific event when the narrative needs a change.

items.spanish: Cuando era niño, mi abuela preparaba una receta tradicional cada domingo.
items.english: When I was a child, my grandmother used to prepare a traditional recipe every Sunday.

items.spanish: La cocina olía a pan recién hecho y toda la familia esperaba la comida.
items.english: The kitchen smelled of freshly baked bread and the whole family waited for the meal.

items.spanish: Mi abuela había heredado la receta de su madre, que la preparaba de la misma manera.
items.english: My grandmother had inherited the recipe from her mother, who prepared it in the same way.

items.spanish: Un domingo cambiamos la receta porque no teníamos todos los ingredientes.
items.english: One Sunday we changed the recipe because we did not have all the ingredients.

sections.content: Use the imperfect for repeated habits and background description; use a completed past event when something happened once and changed the situation.
